description: WI-8 labeled fixture for validating the v3 code-reviewer LLM judge. 20 cases (10 clean / 10 violating) targeting LLM-only rule IDs (the deterministic half is already trusted and is NOT what this gate measures). goal_met convention: a case is 'met' (judge says clean) iff the LLM emits NO critical/warning finding — this measures the judge's DETECTION accuracy, decoupled from the verdict policy (WI-9). Run scripts/record_code_reviewer_validation.py with an API key to populate verdicts.json; the CI test replays the recorded verdicts through meta.judge_validation.validate_judge and asserts TPR/TNR >= 0.90.
detection_convention: goal_met = no critical/warning LLM findings (notes/info do not count as failure detection). This isolates judge detection (WI-8) from verdict-policy calibration (WI-9).

cases.description: A tautological test (assert s == s) in tests/trust/ — asserts nothing, violates TAP-1. LLM-judged (no AST detector for tautology).
A service that invokes the LLM but never calls eval_capture.record — violates H5 (record every LLM call). LLM-judged.
A service module that DEFINES a trust-kernel verdict type (BaseModel) instead of placing it in trust/ — violates AP-1. LLM-judged (no AST detector).
A component returning a raw dict for a non-trivial output instead of a Pydantic model — violates V6. LLM-judged.
A graph node carrying ~20 lines of domain logic (routing, scoring, prompt rendering, verdict) instead of delegating to components/ — violates AP-5 (thin wrappers, <=10-15 lines). LLM-judged.
A meta/ metric function returns 0.0 when the denominator is zero instead of None — fabricates a metric from no data, violates AP-6. LLM-judged.
A TSX form with an <input type=email> that has no label or aria-label — WCAG 2.2 AA violation, FD4. LLM-judged (no TS a11y detector).
A TSX component that calls a cloud API directly from the browser with a hardcoded bearer credential — FE-AP anti-pattern, FD7 critical. LLM-judged.
Middleware that generates a trace_id with crypto.randomUUID instead of flowing it verbatim from upstream — violates the FD1 trace_id rule. LLM-judged.
A PostToolUse hook that emits a 'block' decision and exits non-zero — violates HOOK-1 (PostToolUse never blocks the edit). LLM-judged.
A clean trust-kernel enum — pure data, no I/O, no logging, no upward imports.
A clean service config that selects profiles by tier (H2), no trust types, no components import, no langgraph.
A clean component router with a Pydantic output model (V6), deterministic heuristics (V2), no peer imports, no framework import.
A clean thin orchestration node that delegates all logic to components/ (AP-5), no domain logic in the node.
A clean meta/ metric that returns None when undecidable (AP-6 respected), no orchestration import (AP-4).
A clean accessible TSX form — labelled input, no cloud calls, no secrets in the bundle.
A clean frontend hook that imports an SDK only via an adapter (FD1), no trace_id generation, no JWT in browser storage.
A clean middleware auth passthrough — no cloud credentials held, trace_id flows verbatim, SDK imports confined to adapters/.
A clean PreToolUse safety-only hook — thin, fail-safe on malformed input (HOOK-3), never blocks the edit (HOOK-1 respected).
A clean .j2 prompt with the naming convention and no numeric thresholds baked into the template (config-split respected).
